newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABARE slices Australia 96/97 gold forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABARE slices Australia 96/97 gold forecasts.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday it had cut its forecasts for Australian gold production and exports for the current year to June 30, 1997.

ABARE said in its September quarter commodities bulletin that it had cut its production forecast for 1996/97 to 297 tonnes from the 300 tonnes it forecast in its June quarter bulletin. It also cut its Australian gold export forecast for 1996/97 to 333.0 tonnes from the 340.2 tonnes forecast in June.
ABARE said the 297 tonne 1996/97 production forecast compared with actual production in 1995/96 of 272.3 tonnes.
"In contrast to South Africa's gold sector, gold production in Australia is forecast to increase significantly after the slow growth of the early 1990s," ABARE said.
"The production increases are being underpinned by a rapid expansion of gold reserves, which reached 4,263 tonnes in 1995, an increase of over 1,200 tonnes in three years," it said.
"The growth in reserves has largely been the result of a consolidation of the Australian gold industry as it pursues prospects with a larger average size and longer mine life."
ABARE said its 333.0 tonne Australian export forecast for 1996/97 compared with actual export of 341.0 tonnes in 1995/96, which was itself up on the 284.0 tonnes exported in 1994/95.
It said about 30 tonnes of the sharp increase in 1995/96 came from export of gold stocks previously accumulated in Australia.
"In 1996/97, gold export volumes are forecast to return to a more normal trend, in line with Australian refined gold production," ABARE said.

"As a result, gold exports of Australian origin are forecast to fall to 284 tonnes, and the total export volume of gold is expected to decline by just over 2 percent to 333 tonnes," it said. "Exports of gold of overseas origin are anticipated to increase by over 35 percent to 49 tonnes in 1996/97," it said.

"The forecast decline in total gold export volumes and the gold price in Australian dollar terms mean that total Australian gold export earnings are forecast to fall by over three percent to A$5.4 billion in 1996/97," ABARE said.
ABARE forecast the price of gold would fall to A$506 per ounce in 1996/97 from A$514 in 1995/96, with the U.S. dollar price falling to US$391 per ounce from US$392.
